title: Perfect-source internal Hom inherits the single-complex base-change stalk condition
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use the ordinary tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], derived by K-flat resolutions with flat terms, and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms, put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and write $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ for the projections. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, $K'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'})$, and $\phi:Lh^*K\to K'$.
For every geometric point $\bar z$ of $X'$, put $\bar x=h\bar z$, $\bar y'=f'\bar z$, $\bar y=f\bar x$, $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}$, and $C=\mathcal O_{X',\bar z}$. Assume the canonical maps
$$\beta^i_{\phi,\bar z}:H^i(K_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C\longrightarrow H^i(K'_{\bar z})$$
are isomorphisms for every $\bar z$ and every $i\in\mathbf Z$ [def-sfb-space-single-complex-stalk-condition]. The maps are induced by $K_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to K_{\bar x}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C\to K'_{\bar z}$ and $C$-linear extension on cohomology.
For every perfect $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, meaning etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], put
$$J=R\mathcal Hom(P,K),\qquad J'=R\mathcal Hom(Lh^*P,K').$$
Then $J,J'$ have quasi-coherent cohomology, and the canonical map
$$\psi:Lh^*J\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom(Lh^*P,Lh^*K)\xrightarrow{R\mathcal Hom(1,\phi)}J'$$
satisfies the same stalk condition: every $\beta^i_{\psi,\bar z}$ is an isomorphism. The first arrow is the evaluation transpose of $Lh^*J\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lh^*P\simeq Lh^*(J\otimes^{\mathbf L}P)\to Lh^*K$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, boundedness of $K,K'$, flatness of $f,g$, or direct-image assertion is assumed.

proof.text: Write $L=Lh^*$ and $H(P,N)=R\mathcal Hom(P,N)$. Let $\{U_k\to X\}$ be an etale covering on whose members $P$ is represented by strict-perfect complexes $F_k^\bullet$, put $U'_k=U_k\times_XX'$ (an etale covering of $X'$) and let $h_k:U'_k\to U_k$, $j_k:U_k\to X$, $j'_k:U'_k\to X'$ be the projections, so $hj'_k=j_kh_k$. The composition comparisons and the 2-isomorphism clause of the monoidal comparison node give $(LP)|_{U'_k}=Lj'^*_kLh^*P\cong Lh_k^*Lj_k^*P=Lh_k^*(P|_{U_k})$, the restrictions being the exact localization pullbacks. The strict-perfect pullback model applied to $h_k$ and $F_k^\bullet$ then identifies $Lh_k^*(P|_{U_k})$ with the termwise pullback $h_k^*F_k^\bullet$, a strict-perfect complex with the same bounds, ranks and retraction identities. Hence $LP$ is perfect. Put $E=H(P,\mathcal O_X)$. Perfect duality makes $E$ perfect. The perfect-source case of the quasi-coherence theorem, applied to $(P,\mathcal O_X)$, $(P,K)$ and $(LP,K')$, gives $E,J,J'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ on their respective spaces. Here $\mathcal O_X$ is itself a quasi-coherent module, and no lower bound is used.

proof.text: Let $e:E\otimes^{\mathbf L}P\to\mathcal O_X$ be evaluation. Perfect duality gives the natural evaluation isomorphisms $a_N:E\otimes^{\mathbf L}N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P,N)$. The perfect-source pullback comparison at $N=\mathcal O_X$, followed by the unit comparison, gives an isomorphism $r:LE\xrightarrow{\sim}H(LP,\mathcal O_{X'})$. Its defining transpose is the pairing $e_L:LE\otimes^{\mathbf L}LP\xrightarrow{t^{-1}}L(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}P)\xrightarrow{L(e)}L\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{X'}$. Thus perfect duality for $LP$ gives the isomorphism $b:LE\otimes^{\mathbf L}K'\xrightarrow{r\otimes1}H(LP,\mathcal O_{X'})\otimes^{\mathbf L}K'\xrightarrow{\sim}J'$. Write $T=E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$, $T'=LE\otimes^{\mathbf L}K'$, and $a=a_K:T\xrightarrow{\sim}J$.

Apply tensor inheritance to $E$, $K$, $K'$ and $\phi$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given cartesian square, quasi-coherence of $K,K'$ and the stalk condition for $\phi$, together with the quasi-coherence of $E$ proved in step 1. It supplies the stalk condition for $\lambda:LT\xrightarrow{t}LE\otimes^{\mathbf L}LK\xrightarrow{1\otimes\phi}T'$. In particular $\beta^i_{\lambda,\bar z}$ is invertible for every geometric $\bar z$ and integer $i$.

We verify $\psi\circ L(a)=b\circ\lambda$ rather than choosing any isomorphism between their objects. Suppress the canonical associators, unitors and the symmetry that moves the last $P$ next to $E$. Uncurrying $a_N$ gives $e\otimes1_N$; uncurrying $b$ gives $e_L\otimes1_{K'}$. By the evaluation-transpose definition of the pullback comparison, uncurrying $\psi\circ L(a)$ gives $\phi\circ L(\operatorname{ev}_{P,K}\circ(a\otimes1_P))$ after the inverse tensor comparison. Substitute $\operatorname{ev}_{P,K}\circ(a\otimes1_P)=e\otimes1_K$. The strong symmetric monoidal identities for $L$ and the formula for $e_L$ in step 2 identify this composite with $e_L\otimes\phi$. Uncurrying $b\circ\lambda$ gives $(e_L\otimes1_{K'})\circ(1_{LE}\otimes\phi\otimes1_{LP})$, which is also $e_L\otimes\phi$ by bifunctoriality of tensor. The closed adjunction is a bijection, so the two curried arrows agree. All constraints here are those fixed by the cited comparisons; in particular their symmetries include the cochain signs.

proof.text:
Fix $\bar z,i$ and put $D=A\otimes_RB$. The definition of the canonical stalk comparison is natural in both coefficients: apply stalks, derived tensor over $R$ with $B$, cohomology and scalar extension to $C$ to the equality in step 4. It gives
$$\beta^i_{\psi,\bar z}\circ\bigl(H^i(a_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_D C\bigr)=H^i(b_{\bar z})\circ\beta^i_{\lambda,\bar z}.$$
The two maps induced by $a,b$ are isomorphisms, since functors preserve inverses. The right-hand stalk comparison is an isomorphism by step 3. Composing this equality with the inverse of the left vertical map proves that $\beta^i_{\psi,\bar z}$ is an isomorphism, as required.
